Create an ORIGINAL FORMA exercise illustration atlas, landscape exactly 1536x1024 pixels, THREE COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, SIX equally sized separate cells. White background, subtle shadows, accurate charcoal/gray gym clothing and apparatus with tiny lime green accent. Clean modern detailed fitness manual drawing. NO WORDS, labels, numbers, logos, borders, watermarks. One fully clothed adult athlete per cell, anatomically exactly TWO arms and TWO legs, realistic plausible grip and support. Entire person, bar ends and equipment contained in own 512x512 cell with at least 30px blank margin. Do not merge or overlap cells. Emphasize the explicit pose below; correct equipment, support, grip and variation is essential. Every cell uses single representative phase, no duplicated bodies.

ROW 1 COLUMN 1: Kong Curl. Kong curl alternating dumbbells: standing front three-quarter, RIGHT elbow tucked low beside waist, right forearm flexed diagonally across torso so right dumbbell reaches upper middle chest THUMB FIRST. Right forearm pronated obliquely 45 degrees, knuckles face up/out. LEFT arm hangs down holding second dumbbell, only slight elbow bend. Upper arms stay low; asymmetrical cross-body curl, not bilateral high pull.

ROW 1 COLUMN 2: Kreis Press DB. Kreis press forward phase: seated supported on 45 DEGREE incline bench, arms fully extended forward perpendicular to torso, two dumbbells meeting side by side at chest height. BOTH PALMS FACE UP toward ceiling, wrists supinated, show undersides and thumbs outward, elbows almost straight. View from side front to establish 45degree bench and palms-up extension.

ROW 1 COLUMN 3: Landmine Squat to Press. Landmine squat-to-press FINISH: athlete standing fully upright STRAIGHT knees/hips, leaning slightly forward; BOTH arms fully extended diagonally overhead cupping free barbell end together. Entire bar slopes down to visible floor landmine anchor in front. Feet flat slightly wide, biceps close to ears. No squat in this phase.

ROW 2 COLUMN 1: Lat Pull DB. Lat Pull DB: athlete standing hip-hinged with torso forward near horizontal, knees soft, holds TWO dumbbells. Both upper and lower arms nearly straight with only slight 15degree elbow bends, swept BACKWARD alongside hips, dumbbells near back hips. Show side view and long almost straight arms behind torso; no flexed elbow row.

ROW 2 COLUMN 2: Lat Pull Down (Straight Back). Straight-back lat pulldown: seated perfectly upright at overhead cable machine, legs under thigh pad, medium wide overhand grip long bar pulled IN FRONT of face to upper chest. Cable rises to overhead pulley. Bar below chin at collarbone, shoulders down, no backward lean or behind-neck bar.

ROW 2 COLUMN 3: Leg Extension Isometric. Isometric leg extension against immovable machine: seated on leg-extension machine with back support, one shin pressing outward into thick FIXED roller pad at lower shin near ankle; knee is held approximately 45degrees bent. Roller supported by rigid bolted locked arm clearly connected to machine base, not free-floating. Both hands hold side seat handles, other foot grounded. Representative resisted hold.

cells.title: Kong Curl
cells.guideText: This exercise is somewhat similar to a cable curl and a cable crossover. But instead of a chest/biceps exercise, this exercise targets the brachialis muscle, responsible for that broad arm when viewed from a front view. During the exercise, maintain a pronated forearm position with starting position of approx. 45 degree pronated. Start with slightly bend elbows and alternately curl until your hands (your thumb first) meet your upper middle chest (similar to how Kong hits his chest, thus the name of this exercise).

cells.title: Landmine Squat to Press
cells.guideText: Bar Position: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or a secure corner. Stance: Stand facing the barbell with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width. Turn your toes out 10–35 degrees to allow for better pelvic movement and depth. Grip: Cup the free end of the barbell with both hands (fingers interlaced or overlapping) and hold it at mid-chest level, just below the collarbone. Descent: Brace your core and sit back into a squat, keeping your chest up and weight on your heels. Depth: Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor. A good reference is when your elbows touch the tops of your thighs or just inside your knees. Posture: Ensure your back remains flat and your spine neutral throughout the movement. Drive: Powerfully drive through your heels to stand up. Use the momentum from your legs to "thrust" the weight upward. Extension: In one fluid motion, press the bar overhead until your arms are fully extended. At the top, your biceps should be near your ears. The "Lean": As you reach the top of the press, lean slightly forward into the bar to encourage proper upward rotation of the shoulder blades and avoid lower back arching. Slowly lower the barbell back to chest height in a controlled manner before immediately beginning the next repetition.
